title: CirSTAG: Circuit Stability Analysis on Graph-based Manifolds
problem: Circuit stability (sensitivity) analysis requires numerous time-consuming simulations to estimate how parameter variations (gate sizes, capacitance) impact circuit performance. Existing methods struggle with scalability for large integrated circuits.
motivation: Accurate and efficient stability analysis of modern ICs is critical for design automation and predicting the robustness of circuits under manufacturing variations.
method: CirSTAG uses graph neural networks (AI systems that understand connections between circuit components) to measure circuit stability without running many simulations. It calculates a stability score—the local Lipschitz constant, which measures how much the circuit responds to small input changes—for each component and connection, considering both the network structure and how changing component values affects behavior. When nearby components on the input map to distant components on the output (mapping distortion), this reveals poor stability and identifies the most critical circuit elements.
key_novelty: For the first time, it applies spectral manifold analysis using graph neural networks to circuit stability, enabling scalable robustness assessment through local Lipschitz constants instead of running countless simulations.
contributions: Novel spectral framework for analyzing GNN stability using input/output graph-based manifolds and mapping distortion detection
Scalable method to identify critical (sensitive) circuit elements without extensive simulation
Empirical validation on timing prediction tasks demonstrating accurate stability estimation under diverse parameter variations

metrics.accuracy: accurate stability estimation across timing prediction tasks

primary_theme: GNN-based circuit stability analysis via spectral manifolds
